title: Linear Algebra Done Right
summary: This is a comprehensive mathematics textbook focused on abstract vector spaces and linear maps, intended for students who have had a previous introductory exposure to the subject. It emphasizes deep conceptual understanding through rigorous definitions, theorems, and proofs, notably avoiding the use of determinants until the final chapters.

title: Book of Proof
summary: This textbook provides a comprehensive introduction to mathematical proof techniques, covering fundamental topics such as set theory, logic, counting, and various methods of proof including induction and contradiction. It is designed for undergraduate mathematics students to transition from computational mathematics to rigorous proof-based reasoning.

title: Principles of Mathematical Analysis
summary: This is a classic undergraduate-level textbook on real analysis by Walter Rudin. It covers fundamental topics including the real and complex number systems, topology, sequences and series, differentiation, integration, and the Lebesgue theory.

title: Mathematics for Economists
summary: This document is the table of contents and introductory material for a comprehensive textbook on mathematical methods used in economic theory. It covers foundational topics including one-variable calculus, linear algebra, and the calculus of several variables, with specific applications to economic models.

title: Essential Mathematics for Economic Analysis
summary: This document is the front matter and table of contents for the fourth edition of a comprehensive mathematics textbook designed for economics students. It outlines the foundational algebraic, functional, and logical topics covered in the text, ranging from basic arithmetic to advanced mathematical modeling.

title: Real Analysis: Compactness, Continuity, and Differentiation
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in real analysis, including the properties of compact sets in Euclidean space, the Heine-Borel theorem, and the continuity of linear operators. The document also provides proofs for the Lipschitz continuity of linear maps and demonstrates that differentiability implies continuity.

title: Probability Theory Lecture Notes
summary: These notes provide a comprehensive overview of foundational probability theory, covering axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' Rule, and random variables. They also detail the properties of CDFs, joint distributions, expectation, variance, and the law of iterated expectations.

title: Analysis: Guided Exercises
summary: This document provides a series of guided exercises covering fundamental topics in real analysis, including topology in R^n, compactness, multivariate differential calculus, and the inverse/implicit function theorems. It emphasizes proof techniques and the development of rigorous arguments for graduate-level economics students.

title: Linear Algebra: Guided Review and Exercises
summary: This document provides a guided review of core linear algebra topics including linear systems, rank-nullity, linear maps, and diagonalization. summary: This document provides a comprehensive review of linear algebra topics including linear systems, rank, null space, linear maps, eigenvalues, and orthogonality. It combines mini-lectures with worked examples and practice problems, including detailed solutions for most exercises.

title: Real Analysis Guided Exercises
summary: This document contains a series of guided exercises covering topology, continuity, compactness, differentiability, and the inverse/implicit function theorems in Euclidean space. summary: This document contains a set of linear algebra exercises covering systems of equations, vector subspaces, diagonalization, and matrix definiteness. Each exercise is followed by detailed step-by-step solutions.

title: Analysis in Euclidean Spaces
summary: These lecture notes provide a rigorous foundation for analysis in Euclidean spaces, covering real number completeness, topology, continuity, differentiation, and integration. The text emphasizes the application of these mathematical tools to economic modeling, including existence proofs, local approximation, and comparative statics.

title: Linear Algebra Lecture Notes
summary: These lecture notes provide a comprehensive introduction to linear algebra, covering vector spaces, linear maps, determinants, eigenvalues, and inner product spaces. The text emphasizes the structural relationships between abstract linear maps and their matrix representations, with a focus on applications relevant to economics.

title: Part III: Optimization, Convexity and Correspondences
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of optimization theory, covering convex geometry, concave functions, and optimization in Euclidean space. It further explores equality and inequality-constrained optimization, duality, parameterized optimization, and fixed-point theorems, with specific applications to economic models.

title: Part IV: Probability Theory
summary: These notes provide a comprehensive overview of probability theory, covering fundamental concepts from probability spaces and random variables to expectation, conditional expectation, and stochastic convergence. The document bridges elementary computational methods with rigorous measure-theoretic foundations, specifically tailored for economics PhD students.

title: Introduction to Linear Algebra: Vector Spaces and Linear Maps
summary: These notes provide a foundational overview of linear algebra, covering vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, and spanning sets. The document further explains the concepts of basis, change of basis, and the representation of linear maps as matrices.

title: Linear Algebra: Rank, Nullity, and Change of Basis
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including the Rank-Nullity Theorem, invariant subspaces, and the mechanics of change of basis for linear transformations. It also introduces the definitions of matrix equivalence and similarity, as well as the concepts of direct sums and determinants.

title: Linear Algebra: Invariant Subspaces, Eigenvalues, and Inner Product Spaces
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including invariant subspaces, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and the process of diagonalization. The document also introduces inner product spaces, defining norms, orthogonality, and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.

title: Linear Algebra: Orthonormal Bases, Spectral Theorem, and Quadratic Forms
summary: These notes cover fundamental concepts in linear algebra, including the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the Gram-Schmidt process for orthonormalization, and the Spectral Theorem for real symmetric matrices. The document also explains the application of the Spectral Theorem to simplify quadratic forms and provides criteria for determining the definiteness of matrices using principal minors.
